title: Four Concepts, Four Types: Levels, Boundaries, and a Translation Protocol for Intelligence, Human Intelligence, Artificial Intelligence, and AGI（四个概念，四种类型：智能、人类智能、人工智能、通用人工智能的层次、边界与转译协议）
description: This repository contains the manuscript (Chinese primary edition and English edition, LaTeX + PDF) and bibliographies for a concept analysis of the four central terms of the AGI debate. The paper advances three claims. (1) A typology: the four terms are four different concept types — intelligence is a capacity concept, human intelligence a sample concept, artificial intelligence an artifact concept, and AGI a reference-frame concept; each type has a different form of "completed definition", and the popular narrow–general–super ladder is a narrative device that strings four concept types on a single line. (2) A layered structure: within each concept, distinguish the ontological layer (what it is), the epistemic layer (what evidence supports attributing it to a system), and the methodological layer (what procedure detects it); the chronic root of definitional disputes is three illicit slides — operationalism (measurement passing as definition), the mereological fallacy (mechanism passing as the location of a capacity), and criterion promotion (artifact criteria passing as conceptual content), each diagnosed on verbatim quotations graded by assertion strength. (3) A translation protocol: a table mapping six kinds of engineering observations (circuit ablations, probes, feature-space geometry, benchmark scores, economic-substitution task sets, training phase transitions) to the conceptual claims they license, each row with conditions of validity, governed by three general rules (attribution preservation, conditions travel, layer placement) and a catalogue of four illicit forms (locational, part-whole misattribution, promotion, universalization). The paper closes with the four terms' positions in the human-referential theory of AGI, falsifiability clauses, and an appendix mapping the argument onto the Chinese-language context (terminology history, policy vocabulary drift, interlocutor locations).
notes: Chinese primary edition (paper_zh) and English edition (paper_en) are parallel translations; Chinese-language bibliography entries in the English edition follow sinological convention (pinyin authors, translated titles, [in Chinese] tag).
